metadata.file_name: Brit J of Edu Psychol - 2024 - Cheung - A machine‐learning model of academic resilience in the times of the COVID‐19.pdf
metadata.title: A machine‐learning model of academic resilience in the times of the COVID‐19 pandemic: Evidence drawn from 79 countries/economies in the PISA 2022 mathematics study

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata covering 79 countries/economies and constructs a binary outcome (academically resilient vs non-academically resilient) from ESCS and mathematics performance. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so it is unclear whether complex survey design was incorporated into model estimation and evaluation. The authors do, however, implement a 10-fold cross-validation procedure with an equal-distribution regrouping strategy to maintain the ARS/NRS ratio within folds, and they preprocess each fold/module independently to reduce information leakage. For analysts replicating this work, the recommended approach is to use PISA-provided sampling weights (and replicate weights if available) when estimating performance and feature contributions, but the paper’s ML pipeline (random forest + SHAP) does not describe a weight-aware implementation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Uses PISA 2022 mathematics study data from 79 countries/economies. Defines academic resilience using an international perspective operationalization: (1) select students in the bottom quarter of ESCS within their country/economy; (2) among these ESCS-disadvantaged students, select those whose mathematics performance is in the top quarter across the 79 countries/economies; (3) code academically resilient students (ARS)=1 and non-academically resilient students (NRS)=0. The final analytic sample is 147,658 ESCS-disadvantaged students, comprising 18,500 ARS and 129,158 NRS. For missing data, the pipeline applies k-nearest neighbour (kNN) imputation within each data module/fold during preprocessing.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (15-year-olds), international resilience definition across 79 countries/economies
main_findings.target_variable: Academic resilience in mathematics (ARS=1 vs NRS=0)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest (10-fold cross-validation, average): Accuracy=90.54%, ROC-AUC=96.79%, Precision=93.13%, Recall=87.58%, F-measure=90.26%. Optimal feature subset: top 35 features (F-measure ~90.35% at 35 features; convergent after 35). SHAP effect sizes reported for key features (e.g., self-efficacy SHAP ~0.15–0.20; grade repetition largest negative SHAP > -0.4).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics the study leveraged mathematics self-efficacy, familiarity with math concepts, mathematics anxiety, family support for self-learning, and ICT self-efficacy to classify academic resilience (ARS vs NRS), finding that the random forest achieved strong discrimination (ROC-AUC=96.79%) and identified 35 key features with SHAP-based contributions. This indicates that strengthening self-efficacy and ICT-related competencies, while reducing risk factors such as grade repetition, lateness, and truancy, may help mitigate disadvantage-linked mathematics underperformance, though the results are predictive and cross-sectional so causal effects cannot be inferred.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2022 mathematics microdata from 79 countries/economies and defines academic resilience internationally as ESCS-disadvantaged students (bottom quarter within country) who also show high mathematics performance (top quarter across countries). The final analytic sample contains 147,658 ESCS-disadvantaged students (18,500 ARS; 129,158 NRS), and the dependent variable is binary (ARS=1, NRS=0). A random forest classifier is trained with recursive feature elimination to select an optimal subset, and SHAP values are used to quantify each feature’s contribution; the pipeline uses kNN imputation for missing values and selects PVMATH1 as the mathematics performance PV. Model evaluation via 10-fold cross-validation reports average Accuracy=90.54%, ROC-AUC=96.79%, Precision=93.13%, Recall=87.58%, and F-measure=90.26%. The paper does not report survey-weight usage, and SHAP provides feature contribution rather than causal impact, so policy implications should be framed as correlational and predictive.
